attacks.claim: The hold-ready text tells whoever holds the phone that a hold exists, at a named branch, with a pickup deadline. The statute forbids disclosing requested materials, and the plan's 'reveals nothing' claim overstates the protection. The city attorney reviewed only the provider contract clause, not the message content or disclosure to shared or reassigned numbers.
attacks.evidence: "Riverbend Library: 1 item is ready for pickup at Eastside Branch until Nov 4." / "A reassigned number or shared phone reveals nothing about what the patron requested." — ABSENT: attorney sign-off on message content and on disclosure to shared or reassigned numbers.

attacks.claim: New sign-ups who pick SMS get NOTICE_PREV=phone, but CallNotify ends 2027-03-31 and will not be renewed. A STOP or rollback after that date sends these patrons to a dead channel, which breaks the no-loss constraint. The plan also claims they return to exactly their prior channel, which is false because they never had a phone channel.
attacks.evidence: "new sign-ups who pick SMS get `phone`" / "restore `NOTICE_PREV` (email or phone call; print notice once CallNotify has ended)" / "Patrons who enrolled after launch end up on exactly the channel they had before."

attacks.claim: The receiver's DB grants cannot support its specified behaviour. It needs SELECT to match numbers and read NOTICE_PREV, it must write a staff circulation note with no granted table, and it needs UPDATE on message_queue to record delivery status. The 'consecutive failures' counter has no storage defined.
attacks.evidence: "UPDATE only on `borrower_message_transport_preferences` and `borrower_attributes`, and INSERT only on `message_queue` and `messages`" vs "adds a circulation note visible to staff" and "After 2 consecutive failures"

attacks.claim: STOP switch-back and failure fallback depend on one self-hosted receiver with no stated redundancy, health check, alerting, retry or on-call owner. During an outage, callbacks are lost and patrons are never switched back, which breaks the no-loss constraint.
attacks.evidence: "A webhook receiver (~150 lines, on the existing Koha app server behind the existing nginx/TLS) exposes a single rate-limited POST path" — ABSENT: alerting, health check, provider retry policy for callbacks.

attacks.claim: Fallback runs only on an explicit undelivered/failed callback. Silent drops, missing delivery receipts and carrier filtering of unregistered or pending 10DLC traffic never trigger it, so those hold notices are lost.
attacks.evidence: "on an `undelivered`/`failed` status callback, the receiver queues the same notice on the patron's `NOTICE_PREV` channel" — ABSENT: timeout or missing-receipt handling.

attacks.claim: Matching a SMS number to stored patron numbers has no normalisation rule (for example E.164). A format mismatch means the matching patron is not switched back and keeps losing notices.
attacks.evidence: "switches every patron whose SMS number matches" — ABSENT: phone number normalisation rule.

attacks.claim: Only public launch is gated on 10DLC approval. The week 3 staff pilot could run before approval, which is 1–3 weeks from the Oct 20 submission. Pilot texts may be blocked by carriers, so the pilot result would be misleading, and no slip contingency exists.
attacks.evidence: "The 'Library account notifications' campaign was submitted Oct 20; typical approval is 1–3 weeks. Public launch is gated on approval." / "Week 3: staff pilot. 40 staff cardholders opt in"

attacks.claim: The $600 SMS budget is enforced only by a $450 alert with no hard cap or enrolment limit. At the stated $0.011 per text, the cap is exceeded at about 54,500 texts/month. Systemwide OPAC enablement in week 4 makes this reachable.
attacks.evidence: "a provider spend alert fires at $450" / "Assumed uptake: 50% of phone patrons + 10% of email patrons" — ABSENT: hard spend cap or automatic opt-in limit.

attacks.claim: The one-segment, $0.011 cost model assumes GSM-7 for all messages. Spanish accented vowels á, í, ó and ú are not in GSM-7, so Spanish texts switch to UCS-2 and split into multiple segments. No Spanish text is supplied, so the claim is unverified.
attacks.evidence: "Template (English, plus Spanish for patrons whose preferred language is Spanish, via `TranslateNotices`), GSM-7, one segment"

attacks.claim: Spanish-preferring patrons get the hold notice in Spanish, but the enrolment confirmation and HELP auto-reply are English only. The plan does not say they are translated, so these patrons receive opt-in and STOP/HELP guidance they may not read.
attacks.evidence: "Riverbend Library: you'll get a text when holds are ready for pickup. Msg frequency varies..." / "Riverbend Library hold notices. Call 555-0142 or visit riverbendlibrary.org/sms. Reply STOP to cancel."

attacks.claim: The plan does not say whether the SMS transport adds to or replaces NOTICE_PREV for 'Hold filled'. This determines whether patrons get duplicate notices or depend solely on the fallback path.
attacks.evidence: "Patron messaging preferences already support an SMS transport per notice type; we enable it for 'Hold filled' only."

attacks.claim: A public internet-facing POST endpoint writes to patron tables, and signature verification is the only stated control. The plan does not say how the signing key is stored or rotated, or whether verification fails closed.
attacks.evidence: "verifies the provider's request signature" — ABSENT: signing key storage, rotation and fail-closed behaviour.

attacks.claim: Webhook logs keep the last four digits of phone numbers, which still link a number to a patron record. No log retention period or access control is stated.
attacks.evidence: "phone numbers as the last 4 digits" — ABSENT: log retention and access controls.

attacks.claim: SMS_CONSENT and NOTICE_PREV persist with no retention or purge rule, including after patrons leave or opt out.
attacks.evidence: "Patron attribute `SMS_CONSENT` records the date and source (opac/desk)." — ABSENT: retention period and purge rule.

attacks.claim: Desk-entered consent is recorded without a documented patron affirmation or consent wording, so the consent record cannot be shown to meet carrier or TCPA expectations.
attacks.evidence: "staff set it at the desk when the patron asks and provides a mobile number" — ABSENT: desk consent wording.

attacks.claim: Switching every patron who shares a STOPping number back to their own channel affects family members without their knowledge. The plan does not address this.
attacks.evidence: "switches every patron whose SMS number matches (family members can share a phone)"

attacks.claim: The claim that switching providers is only a config change conflicts with the plan's own design. The receiver implements provider-specific signature verification and STOP/status handling, and STOP keywords and 10DLC registration would also need reimplementation.
attacks.evidence: "Switching providers later is a config change, not a code change." vs "verifies the provider's request signature" and "~150 lines"

attacks.claim: The rate limit on the callback endpoint may reject provider callbacks during the 09:00 queue burst. Provider retry on 429 or 5xx is unstated, so a STOP could go unrecorded. Provider throughput and 10DLC campaign rate limits are also unaddressed.
attacks.evidence: "exposes a single rate-limited POST path" — ABSENT: callback retry behaviour on HTTP 429 or 5xx, and throughput limits.

attacks.claim: Rollback steps are not atomic. Clearing SMSSendDriver can happen while pending SMS rows remain, and the 15-minute queue job may still send during the re-queue. The script was tested only on staging, not at production scale.
attacks.evidence: "3. Clear `SMSSendDriver`." / "written and tested in week 2 against a staging copy of the patron database"

attacks.claim: The template hardcodes the singular 'item', and the plan does not define plural handling, so counts above 1 would read ungrammatically.
attacks.evidence: "Riverbend Library: 1 item is ready for pickup at Eastside Branch until Nov 4."

attacks.claim: The copy is inconsistent. The notice says 'opt out' while the confirmation and HELP text say 'cancel'.
attacks.evidence: "Reply STOP to opt out, HELP for help." vs "Reply STOP to cancel, HELP for help."

attacks.claim: The new OPAC 'Your messaging' control has no keyboard, screen-reader or contrast testing before the week 4 systemwide enablement.
attacks.evidence: "Week 4, after 10DLC approval: OPAC option enabled systemwide, branch signage"

attacks.claim: The failure-fallback test uses one invalid number, which produces one failure. It cannot exercise the 2-consecutive-failure switch-back threshold.
attacks.evidence: "the failure fallback (one deliberately invalid number)" vs "After 2 consecutive failures it switches the patron back"

attacks.claim: The uptake assumptions (50% and 10%) are unsourced. The 9.2% vs 5.1% expiry comparison is confounded by self-selection into SMS, which the 90-day measure does not control for, so the savings and expiry benefit may not materialise.
attacks.evidence: "Assumed uptake: 50% of phone patrons + 10% of email patrons" / "Uncollected-hold expiry rate: 9.2% for phone-notice patrons vs 5.1% for email"

attacks.claim: One developer must build five deliverables over four weeks, and the receiver has no named on-call owner after launch.
attacks.evidence: "Team: library systems developer (1), circulation lead (0.5) · 4 weeks" — ABSENT: named post-launch owner for the webhook receiver.
